scope.summary: Reconciled the formal display-transfer evidence guard with the newly adopted in-place fixed-function MSAA resolve path. The previous display-transfer source binding still required the removed secondary resolve RenderTexture and Graphics.Blit, which would have caused the first real QA4K camera pre-cull to fail even though QualityBlock4KCapture had already migrated to ResolveAntiAliasedSurface(). Resolve and display-transfer validation are now co-bound so they cannot drift independently again.
scope.whyThisWasPrioritized: This was a real formal-render blocker discovered by cross-checking the capture implementation against its independent color-transfer guard. Leaving it unresolved would prevent actual 3840x2160 evidence from reaching review and would also make gamma/sRGB provenance internally contradictory. Fixing the evidence path has higher score utility than speculative geometry expansion while Unity Runner remains unavailable.

discoveredDefect.oldCaptureImplementation: QualityBlock4KCapture uses bindMS=false, RenderTexture.ResolveAntiAliasedSurface() in-place and direct ReadPixels from msaaTarget.
discoveredDefect.staleGuardBehavior: QualityBlockDisplayTransferIntegrityQA.ValidateCaptureSourceBinding still required resolveDescriptor, resolvedTarget, Graphics.Blit(msaaTarget, resolvedTarget), and readback from resolvedTarget.
discoveredDefect.consequence: During a real QA4K hero render, the display-transfer Camera.onPreCull callback would call ValidateContractConfigOnly(), reject the new capture source, disable the required filmic tonemap in its catch path, and prevent a valid HDR-tonemap receipt from sealing. No Visual Fidelity image could become authoritative.
discoveredDefect.resolution: Updated display-transfer source binding and machine-readable contract to the canonical single-target in-place resolve model, added bindTextureMS/mipmap runtime rejection, and made capture-resolve validation co-validate display-transfer configuration.

changes.effect: Schema/token expectations now describe display-transfer-integrity-v1.1.0. Source binding requires bindMS=false, sRGB target descriptor, ResolveAntiAliasedSurface(), direct ReadPixels from msaaTarget and forbids resolvedTarget/resolveDescriptor/post-tonemap Graphics.Blit reintroduction. Formal targets must also remain bindTextureMS=false and non-mipmapped at pre-cull.

Machine-readable display-transfer contract now defines a single canonical non-HDR sRGB target, in-place fixed-function resolve, direct readback, no secondary resolved target, no post-tonemap shader copy, runtime failure policy and Runner failure injections.

Capture-resolve schema moved to 1.1 and now fail-closed co-validates QualityBlockDisplayTransferIntegrityQA so resolve and gamma/sRGB source assumptions cannot become contradictory in future refactors.
Adds displayTransferContractMustCoValidate=true and cross-contract failure injection requirements while keeping automatic Visual Fidelity points at zero.

unity6: Unity 6 RenderTextureReadWrite documentation states that non-HDR render textures in Linear color space are normally sRGB read/write targets and RenderTexture.sRGB reports that state.
Unity 6 RenderTexture.ResolveAntiAliasedSurface documentation states that omitting the target resolves the antialiased RenderTexture into itself.
Unity 6 RenderTexture.bindTextureMS documentation states that bindTextureMS=true prevents default resolved-surface behavior for multisampled shader binding.

staticRepositoryVerification: Start HEAD to pre-record HEAD compares ahead 5 / behind 0 with merge-base equal to the start HEAD.
Diff before this run record is confined to four UnityProject/Assets Editor/QA files; no Godot path changed.

Final display-transfer source binding no longer requires the removed resolveDescriptor/resolvedTarget/Graphics.Blit capture path and explicitly requires ResolveAntiAliasedSurface plus direct msaaTarget ReadPixels.
Capture-resolve source guard now calls display-transfer contract validation, while the display-transfer guard does not call capture-resolve validation, avoiding recursion.
Both machine-readable contracts retain actual-render-required and zero-auto-point policy.
